Testimony by William Norbert
Governmental Affairs and Communications Manager
In Support of L.D. 1653
An Act to Develop Maine's Credentialed Workforce
May 5, 2025
Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and Distinguished Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs:
My name is Bill Norbert. I am the Governmental Affairs and Communications
Manager at the Finance Authority of Maine (FAME). I am presenting this testimony in support of L.D. 1653, An Act to Develop Maine 's Credentialed Workforce.
We first wish to thank Representative Sargent for sponsoring this bill, as well as
the various cosponsors.
FAME's mission is to enrich business and educational outcomes through relevant,
timely financial support to Maine's people. Our vision is a Maine where all people have access to improved economic outcomes through business growth and education
attainment
This bill would establish within FAME the Maine Credentialed Workforce
Program to support the credentialing needs of current and future participants in the state's
workforce through student loan repayments to eligible persons who are employed in
occupations identified by FAME (with input from experts such as DECD, MDOL, higher education institutions, and others) as needing skilled workers. We are seeking no funding
at this time but instead ask that you help establish this program in statute so that we may
return in the future with proposals for existing FAME programs or new workforce
occupations and legislative proposals to consider including in the program.
FAME has administered a variety of loan and loan repayment programs since
assuming oversight of the state's higher education loan and loan repayment program from
the Maine Department of Education in 1990. It is an honor we take seriously, and we
appreciate the trust you have placed in us. Our aim with this proposal is to get a better handle on the various current and future proposals for loan and loan repayment programs,
l

as well as our existing programs, in a way that is more efficient, cost-effective, and
responsive to our state's current workforce needs.
This session alone, there are at least six separate proposals to create new grant,
loan, or loan repayment programs for FAME to administer. These cover occupations
ranging from lawyers to dentists to loggers and fishermen to recent college graduates employed in the trades (tool loans) to foreign trained physicians and state and federal workers (shutdown loans). If enacted and funded, these concepts would be added to the
six existing grant, loan and loan repayment programs we currently administer: Educators for Maine; Maine Health Professions Loan Program; Maine Health Care Provider Loan Repayment Pilot Program; Maine Veterinary Medicine Loan Program; Maine Dental Education Loan and Loan Repayment Program; the Nursing Education Loan Repayment
Program; and the Foreign Credentialing and Skills Recognition Grant Program. Other
programs listed in statute but never funded by the Legislature or operated by FAME
include: the Social Work Education Loan Repayment Program; Maine Engineers
Recruitment and Retention Program; Future for Youth in Maine Loan Repayment Program (aimed at recent college grads starting technology-based businesses); and the Maine Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) Loan Program.
At a time of reduced state funding and rapidly changing workforce needs, we need a thoughtful and concerted approach to targeting Maine's workforce needs with the limited state appropriations and limited loan and loan repayment funds we have available. The current arrangement is fragmented and inconsistent, with separate programs, eligibility criteria, applications, and constituencies. With your help we can design an overarching and responsive approach that offers more benefit to Maine's workforce and employers and allows our customers to focus on one program with a common application. The solution can be simpler, nimbler, and efficient. If we examine Maine's
evolving workforce needs holistically, we will have a better approach. A concerted effort
will be better than a collection of programs. Plus, the various funding can be pooled together to have more impact.
Each of these separate, existing and new programs can be time-consuming and
administratively burdensome to administer as separate, unique entities. When a new program is added, we must engage in rulemaking, design applications and loan
documents, market, administer, and report on it. This proposal would permit us to harness
our time and resources into one overarching umbrella program. We are proposing a new,
overarching loan repayment program to support the credentialing needs of current and
future participants in the state's workforce. FAME would consult the latest available data
and with experts regarding business, education, labor and workforce needs in prioritizing
targeted professions on a regular basis. FAME would establish by rule eligibility
requirements for the program, which would include, at a minimum:
--That the applicant has received an appropriate certificate, credential of value, or bachelor's degree or graduate degree within 2 years of the date of application [amendment to current bill language needed to extend 2 years to something
2

longer, like 5-10 years and include debt and credentials in addition to two-year, four-year degrees and graduate ones]; --That the applicant has outstanding eligible student loans; and --That the applicant is willing to accept and maintain employment in a priority
occupation position in the state for a minimum of four years in return for
repayment by FAME of a portion of that applicant's student loan debt. We recommend maximum loan repayment amounts available to a participant in the
program be $25,000 per year for a maximum of four years, so long as participants remain
employed in their selected professions and work and live in Maine.
In this challenging budget environment, we are not requesting any state funding
this session for the program. The language in the bill regarding the fund allows FAME to
use internal resources, receive outside funding of various kinds, or eventually receive
appropriations for the program. After the language is on the books, we could present in
future years separate proposals/bills to bring existing FAME programs and new
legislative proposals into this new comprehensive program. That way stakeholders can be
heard and their views and recommendations incorporated.
Additionally, this proposal comports well with FAME's current IT modernization
efforts. When finished, our IT modernization will allow us to make these loan
repayments in an easier, more efficient way, and permit us to better monitor and report on
them.
We hope you will enact this new program and support our efforts to be more
efficient and responsive to Maine's workforce needs. Thank you for your consideration and I would be happy to answer any questions you might have.

Nursing Education Loan Repayment Program

Loan repayment program for nursing educators who must: be a nurse; be currently enrolled in a
master's or doctoral degree program in nursing or have completed a master's or doctoral degree in nursing; possess an outstanding education loan relating to the master's or doctoral nursing degree; and agree to work as full-time nursing faculty in a nursing education program in the state for a

FAME will repay the loan of eligible nurse educators in the amount of up to $20,000 over three

Testimony of Rep. Holly T. Sargent introducing
LD 1653, An Act to Develop Maine's Credentialed Workforce
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and distinguished colleagues of the Joint Standing
Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs, my name is Holly Sargent. I represent House
District 147, which is part of York, and am pleased to present this bill, LD 1653, An Act to
Develop Maine's Credentialed Workforce, on behalf of the Finance Authority of Maine (FAME).
We see various proposals each session to create new student loan and loan repayment programs
to help address Maine's workforce needs. This year alone there are at least six related to FAME.
FAME does a good job administering the ones that are funded and in statute, but there are many
that cannot be funded or enacted. And each new loan or loan repayment that does get enacted
requires substantial time, effort, and cost to set up, promote, create rules for, administer, and report on. There must be a better way.
This bill attempts to get a handle on these various proposals by creating one workforce
credentialing program that could be more easily administered by FAME and respond with
flexibility to the state's changing workforce needs. And there's no cost (yet) associated with the
proposal!
The bill would establish within FAME the Maine Credentialed Workforce Program to support
the credentialing needs of current and future participants in the state's workforce through student
loan repayments to eligible persons who are employed in occupations identified by FAME (with
input from experts such as DECD, MDOL, higher education institutions and others) as needing
skilled workers. This bill is not seeking funding at this time, I instead ask that you help put this
program in statute so that FAME may return in the future with proposals for existing FAME
programs or new workforce occupations to consider including in the program.
Just this session alone, there are six separate proposals to create new grant, loan or loan
repayment programs for FAME to administer. These cover occupations ranging from lawyers to
dentists to loggers and fishermen to recent college graduates employed in the trades (tool loans) to foreign trained physicians and state and federal workers (shutdown loans). If enacted and
